title: The Yu Shu King
altTitles: The Classic of the Pivot of Jade
The True Classic of the Pivot of Jade
dateDisplay: Yuan dynasty (1280–1367), as Legge dates it
attributionNote: The scripture is presented as the teaching of the Heaven-Honoured One who produces universal transformation by the sound of his thunder. Legge, following Wylie, takes the author to have been a Hsüan-yang Dze of the Yuan dynasty, in the time of the Mongol court.
description: The Pivot of Jade is a short revealed scripture on the discipline and refinement of the spirit: the body is carried round by the spirit as the heavens are carried round the North Star, and when the spirit is refined until it is free of every obscuring influence it becomes solid, soft and strong as jade. It is recited in Daoist temples and belongs with the Khing Kâng King and the Yin Fû King among the brief classics that Legge printed as appendixes to his Texts of Taoism.
historicalContext: The text is attributed to the Heaven-Honoured One and was transmitted with a commentary; Legge translates it from the Daozang recension and dates its composition to the Yuan. He printed it, with an introductory notice, as the third appendix to the second volume of The Texts of Taoism (1891).
availabilityNote: Complete. Legge's translation is streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time; it is one printed page, presented here as one chapter with its numbered paragraphs indexed. Legge's introductory notice and the notes printed at the foot of the page are not part of the work.
